3wrrjm9qtr2mySELECT T.CLIENT_ID, T.OPERATION_ID, T.TARGET_TYPE, T.TARGET_NAME, T.CURR_JOB_NAME, TO_NUMBER(BITAND(T.ATTRIBUTES, 131072)), CASE NVL((SELECT J.STATE FROM DBA_SCHEDULER_JOBS J WHERE T.CURR_JOB_NAME = J.JOB_NAME), 'MISSING') WHEN 'MISSING' THEN 4 WHEN 'RUNNING' THEN 1 WHEN 'DISABLED' THEN 2 WHEN 'SCHEDULED' THEN 3 WHEN 'RETRY SCHEDULED' THEN 99 WHEN 'COMPLETED' THEN 99 WHEN 'BROKEN' THEN 99 WHEN 'FAILED' THEN 99 WHEN 'REMOTE' THEN 99 WHEN 'SUCCEEDED' THEN 99 WHEN 'STOPPED' THEN 99 WHEN 'CHAIN_STALLED' THEN 99 ELSE 99 END AS CONSOLIDATED_STATE, CASE NVL(JRD.STATUS, 'MISSING') WHEN 'MISSING' THEN 4 WHEN 'SUCCEEDED' THEN 10 WHEN 'FAILED' THEN 11 WHEN 'STOPPED' THEN CASE WHEN JRD.ADDITIONAL_INFO LIKE '%called by user%' THEN 12 WHEN JRD.ADDITIONAL_INFO LIKE '%window was closed%' THEN 13 WHEN JRD.ADDITIONAL_INFO LIKE 'ORA-01014%' THEN 14 ELSE 15 END ELSE 99 END AS STATUS, NVL(JRD.RUN_DURATION, INTERVAL '0' SECOND), NVL(JRD.CPU_USED, INTERVAL '0' SECOND), NVL(JRD.ERROR#, 0), NVL(JRD.STATUS, 'NO LOG ENTRY') || '(jrd)' AS DBG_STATUS, NVL((SELECT J.STATE FROM DBA_SCHEDULER_JOBS J WHERE T.CURR_JOB_NAME = J.JOB_NAME), 'MISSING') ||'(jobs)' AS DBG_STATE, NVL(JRD.LOG_DATE, TIMESTAMP '2001-01-01 01:01:01.01 +01:01'), NVL(JRD.LOG_ID, 0) FROM KET$_CLIENT_TASKS T, DBA_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS JRD WHERE T.CURR_JOB_NAME IS NOT NULL AND T.CURR_JOB_NAME = JRD.JOB_NAME(+) AND 'SYS' = JRD.OWNER(+)

4g6w9zqy8s9bwSELECT tablespace_name, ROUND(used_percent_of_max, 2) AS used_percent, ROUND(100 - used_percent_of_max, 2) AS free_percent, ROUND(used_gb, 2) AS used_gb, ROUND(max_size_gb, 2) AS total_gb, ROUND(allocated_gb, 2) AS allocated_gb FROM (SELECT df.tablespace_name, SUM(df.bytes - NVL(fs.bytes, 0)) / 1024 / 1024 / 1024 AS used_gb, SUM(df.bytes) / 1024 / 1024 / 1024 AS allocated_gb, SUM(CASE WHEN df.maxbytes = 0 THEN df.bytes ELSE df.maxbytes END) / 1024 / 1024 / 1024 AS max_size_gb, (SUM(df.bytes - NVL(fs.bytes, 0)) / SUM(CASE WHEN df.maxbytes = 0 THEN df.bytes ELSE df.maxbytes END)) * 100 AS used_percent_of_max FROM dba_data_files df LEFT JOIN (SELECT tablespace_name, file_id, SUM(bytes) AS bytes FROM dba_free_space GROUP BY tablespace_name, file_id) fs ON df.tablespace_name = fs.tablespace_name AND df.file_id = fs.file_id WHERE df.tablespace_name IN ('SYSTEM', 'AUDIT_DATA', 'SYSAUX') GROUP BY df.tablespace_name)

Finding 4: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .87 active sessions, 7.55% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .87 active sessions, 7.55% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction in the number of
      COMMIT operations by increasing the size of transactions.

      The application was performing 40320 transactions per minute with an
      average redo size of 9370 bytes per transaction.

   Recommendation 2: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .87 active sessions, 7.55% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------

      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.

      average time per write was 1 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 6.8 M per second for

   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and

      all other activity.

Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .31 active sessions, 2.67% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .31 active sessions, 2.67% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 2.19 active sessions, 18.93% of total activity.

Finding 8: Soft Parse
Impact is .24 active sessions, 2.06% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .24 active sessions, 2.06% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .24 active sessions, 2.06% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.
